record.title: Feed customer writes (comment/like/vote) are completely unthrottled — FeedWriteThrottle is an AnonRateThrottle that skips authenticated customers
record.description: All three customer write endpoints of the store feed — POST /api/stores/public/<slug>/feed/<pk>/comments/, .../like/, .../vote/ — declare FeedWriteThrottle (scope 'store_review', configured 10/hour in settings, intended as antispam). FeedWriteThrottle extends ResilientAnonRateThrottle -> DRF AnonRateThrottle.get_cache_key returns None whenever request.user.is_authenticated is truthy (venv/Lib/site-packages/rest_framework/throttling.py:173-175). CustomerJWTAuthentication returns the Customer object as request.user (authentication.py:72-73) and Customer.is_authenticated is a property returning True (models.py:117-119), so for every request that can reach the handlers (all gated by IsCustomer) the throttle key is None and SimpleRateThrottle.allow_request returns True unconditionally (throttling.py:119-121). The throttle is dead code: one self-registered customer account (POST /api/customer-auth/register/, AllowAny, is_active=True default, access JWT issued immediately without email verification) can post unlimited 600-char comments on any published store feed, toggle likes, and cast poll votes. Sibling code proves intent: StoreReviewThrottle.get_cache_key explicitly buckets POSTs by 'review-customer-<pk>' (stores/views/viewset.py:391-401) and support uses _CustomerScopedThrottle keyed 'c<pk>' (support/views/customer.py:57-64); the customer-auth module's own comment states 'NO se usa AnonRateThrottle porque saltaría la cuota a un comprador autenticado' (customers/views/auth_views.py:164-168). Amplifier: PublicFeedCommentsView.get returns every non-hidden comment with no LIMIT/pagination (feed/views/views.py:214-215), so spamming a post inflates every subsequent public GET of that post. FeedComment has no unique constraint — unlimited comments per account per post; likes/votes are unique per (post, customer) but multi-account inflation is feasible since registration is self-service.
record.root_cause: FeedWriteThrottle subclasses ResilientAnonRateThrottle (DRF AnonRateThrottle) instead of a customer-scoped throttle; AnonRateThrottle.get_cache_key returns None for authenticated request.user, and CustomerJWTAuthentication sets request.user to a Customer whose is_authenticated property returns True — so the throttle can never deny any request that passes IsCustomer.
record.intended_behavior: Customer feed writes should be rate-limited per account (mirroring StoreReviewThrottle's 'review-customer-<pk>' bucket or support's 'c<pk>' bucket) at the configured 'store_review' 10/hour scope, and the public comments listing should be bounded.

trace.description: PublicFeedCommentsView mounted at stores/public/<slug>/feed/<pk>/comments/ (POST gated to IsCustomer via get_permissions); like/vote routes at lines 38-39.
class FeedWriteThrottle(ResilientAnonRateThrottle) with scope='store_review' (line 58) — no get_cache_key override; inherits AnonRateThrottle behavior.
Returns (customer, token) so DRF sets request.user = Customer; also sets request.customer used by IsCustomer.
Property returns True unconditionally (lines 117-119) — Customer counts as authenticated for DRF throttles.
if request.user and request.user.is_authenticated: return None (line 174-175); allow_request returns True when key is None (lines 119-121).

FeedComment.objects.create(post=post, customer=request.customer, body=...) — no rate limit, no dedupe, no per-store quota; same unthrottled pattern in PublicFeedLikeView.post (line 241) and PublicFeedVoteView.post (line 259).
comments = post.comments.filter(is_hidden=False).select_related('customer') returned in full at line 215 — no [:N] cap, no pagination (contrast owner view line 166 which caps at 500).

evidence.description: AnonRateThrottle.get_cache_key returns None for authenticated users; UserRateThrottle (lines 193-202) is the correct authenticated-principal throttle and is not used here.
get_throttles returns FeedWriteThrottle for POST on comments; throttle_classes=[FeedWriteThrottle] on like (line 238) and vote (line 248); permission_classes=[IsCustomer] on all writes.
StoreReviewThrottle.get_cache_key buckets POST by f'review-customer-{customer.pk}' — the known-correct pattern the feed throttle fails to replicate (comment at 392-394 cites FP-04).
_CustomerScopedThrottle keys by f'c{customer.pk}' — second sibling proving customer-scoped throttling is the house pattern.
Comment documents the exact pitfall: 'NO se usa AnonRateThrottle porque saltaría la cuota a un comprador autenticado' — the feed throttle reintroduces it.
Customer.is_active defaults True; CustomerRegisterView (auth_views.py:220-246) issues the session JWT immediately via _session_response with no email_verified gate.
'store_review': '10/hour' — the intended rate exists but is unreachable for authenticated customers.
FeedComment has no unique constraint on (post, customer) — unlimited comments per account; body max_length=600 (line 112).

conditions.description: Attacker holds any customer_access JWT — free self-service registration at /api/customer-auth/register/ (10/hour per IP); is_active=True by default and the access token is issued immediately without email verification.
Target store must have the feed benefit enabled (has_feed / feed_enabled) and a published feed post (is_published=True via _public_post).
Cache (Redis) healthy — irrelevant for the bug itself since the throttle never engages; relevant only to whether the intended 10/hour would have applied.

execution.attacker_perspective: Any internet user who registers a free buyer account on a DAVENT store and wants to spam or skew a store's public feed (/novedades) — comment spam visible to all visitors, like/poll-vote inflation, or unbounded growth of the public comments payload.
payloads: POST /api/stores/public/<slug>/feed/<pk>/comments/ Authorization: Bearer <jwt> {"body":"spam..."} repeated N times (N >> 10)
POST /api/stores/public/<slug>/feed/<pk>/vote/ Authorization: Bearer <jwt> {"option":1} across multiple posts/stores/accounts
instructions: Register a customer account and capture the access JWT from the response body.
Pick any published store with feed enabled; GET /api/stores/public/<slug>/feed/ to enumerate post ids.
POST comments in a loop — every request returns 201; no 429 ever occurs because FeedWriteThrottle.get_cache_key returns None for the authenticated Customer.
Repeat like/vote across many posts and, for count inflation, across many freshly registered accounts (unique (post,customer) constraints do not help comments, which have no constraint at all).
GET the comments endpoint repeatedly to observe the unbounded payload grow with each spammed comment.
execution.observed_result: Source-derived (read-only audit): FeedWriteThrottle.get_cache_key resolves to AnonRateThrottle.get_cache_key -> request.user.is_authenticated is True (Customer property) -> returns None -> SimpleRateThrottle.allow_request returns True for 100% of requests that pass IsCustomer. The 10/hour 'store_review' scope is dead code on all three write endpoints; comment creation has no DB-level dedupe, so a single account can create unlimited FeedComment rows.

remediation.strategy: Replace FeedWriteThrottle with a customer-scoped throttle mirroring StoreReviewThrottle/_CustomerScopedThrottle: subclass SimpleRateThrottle (or reuse DaventProject.throttling._ResilientThrottleMixin) and key the cache by f'c{request.customer.pk}' (fallback IP for anonymous) with scope 'store_review'/'10/hour'. Bound PublicFeedCommentsView.get (e.g. comments.filter(is_hidden=False).select_related('customer')[:200] or paginate), consider a per-store inbound comment quota analogous to SUPPORT_STORE_MSGS_PER_HOUR, and consider requiring email_verified for customer_access issuance if abuse continues.

likelihood.reason: Trivially exploitable by any registered customer — free self-service signup with no email-verification gate, a single Bearer token, and a plain POST loop; the throttle can never fire.

impact.reason: Abuse-class only: public comment spam (owner-moderatable one-by-one via is_hidden/delete), poll/like skew requiring multiple accounts, unbounded comment-list payloads amplifying read cost, and DB row growth. No confidentiality or authorization boundary crossed; comments/likes/votes trigger no emails or notifications.

confidence.reason: Every link verified in current source: throttle class hierarchy, vendored DRF AnonRateThrottle/SimpleRateThrottle semantics, Customer.is_authenticated property, CustomerJWTAuthentication return value, IsCustomer on all writes, unbounded comments queryset, sibling throttle implementations, and the registration flow issuing tokens without verification. Source-only audit; no runtime execution needed since the dead-code path is deterministic.

record.title: Support-chat image attachments bypass all storage quota AND all rate limiting — unbounded R2 growth per paid user
record.description: Every store-scoped image upload consumes the plan quota (Store.storage_used_bytes under select_for_update) or is a bounded staff/platform asset. Chat attachments are the sole exception: upload_chat_image validates (validate_image_file: ≤4MB, content-type allowlist, magic bytes), normalizes to WebP (imaging.normalize_image kind 'chat': ≤1600px, q78→floor 60), and PUTs to the DAVENT R2 bucket under key 'chat/<thread.id>/<uuid>.webp' — but never calls _check_quota/_consume_quota and ChatMessage stores only image_key, so no byte accounting exists anywhere. chat/ keys do not match _STORE_KEY_RE '^stores/(\d+)/' (storage.py:109) so they always land in the DAVENT bucket outside store.storage_used_bytes and outside BYO routing. Worse than the hunter claimed: the supposed 120/hour bound does not exist. ChatSendThrottle and ChatPollThrottle extend DRF ScopedRateThrottle, which reads the scope from view.throttle_scope (venv throttling.py:221) — and 'throttle_scope' appears nowhere in the repository, so self.scope becomes None and allow_request returns True unconditionally; the throttle classes' own scope attributes ('chat', 'chat_send') are shadowed and the settings rates (5000/h, 120/h) are never consulted. The view's throttle_classes=[ChatPollThrottle] also replaces DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES, so there is no fallback anon/user throttle either — /api/chat/send/ is effectively unthrottled. Remaining bounds: IsAuthenticated + chat_enabled gate (paid non-trial plan with has_support_chat, services.py:29-39), input normalization caps, and the annual purge_personal_data cron (default --days 365, only if scheduled — deployment fact). A user on the cheapest paid plan can therefore script unlimited ~350KB WebP objects into operator-owned R2, each also costing synchronous Pillow decode/encode CPU on gunicorn workers.
record.root_cause: upload_chat_image (AdminApp/domains/chat/services/attachments.py:27-45) performs validate_image_file + normalize_image + put_object with no quota check or accounting call; chat keys bypass _STORE_KEY_RE so they never touch store.storage_used_bytes; no per-user/per-thread attachment cap exists in send_message or the viewset; and the ScopedRateThrottle subclasses are dead code because no view defines throttle_scope.
record.intended_behavior: All client-driven object uploads should consume a bounded, plan- or user-scoped storage budget consistent with the quota model used by store images, proofs, feed media and AI-design images — or an equivalent explicit aggregate cap with prompt lifecycle cleanup — and the send endpoint should actually enforce the configured chat_send rate.

trace.description: POST /api/chat/send/ — IsAuthenticated + _gate(chat_enabled paid non-trial plan) + get_throttles appends ChatSendThrottle for action 'send' (lines 69-74). throttle_classes=[ChatPollThrottle] (line 67) replaces DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES.

Both extend ScopedRateThrottle with class attrs scope='chat_send'/'chat' — but ScopedRateThrottle.allow_request sets self.scope=getattr(view,'throttle_scope',None) and returns True when falsy; no view in the repo defines throttle_scope (grep: zero matches), so both throttles always allow.
self.scope = getattr(view, self.scope_attr, None); if not self.scope: return True — the throttle-class 'scope' attribute is ignored; scope must live on the view.

validate_image_file -> imaging.normalize_image(upload,'chat') -> key=f'chat/{thread.id}/{uuid4().hex}.{ext}' -> storage.put_object(key, body, content_type) when storage_configured() else default_storage.save('private/'+key). Zero references to _check_quota/_consume_quota/storage_used_bytes.

'chat/...' does not match _STORE_KEY_RE '^stores/(\d+)/' (line 109) -> backend None -> unconditional DAVENT bucket PUT with CacheControl 'private, max-age=0' (lines 302-311); raises ValueError only on total failure.
Persists ChatMessage.image_key (CharField, models.py:46) — object key only; no size/quota fields, no count cap, no FK-level storage accounting; message rows accumulate unbounded.

Only cleanup path: deletes ChatMessage rows + their attachments older than --days (default 365, line 37) — annual/batch cron, not a real-time bound; active threads' attachments persist for up to a year and scheduling is a deployment fact.

evidence.description: Full function body lines 27-45 contains no quota call; contrasted with store-scoped helpers that call _check_quota/_consume_quota (storage.py:411-431).
_STORE_KEY_RE = re.compile(r'^stores/(\d+)/') — chat keys never match, so _store_id_from_key returns None and BYO/store accounting is bypassed entirely.

ScopedRateThrottle returns True when view lacks throttle_scope; repository-wide grep for 'throttle_scope' returns zero matches — ChatPollThrottle/ChatSendThrottle (and NotificationPollThrottle in AdminApp/domains/notifications/views/viewset.py:40, same dead pattern) never throttle.

'chat': '5000/hour' and 'chat_send': '120/hour' rates exist but are unreachable — ScopedRateThrottle reads scope from the view, not these classes; DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES (lines 75-78) are overridden by view.throttle_classes.
MAX_SIDE_CHAT=1600, WEBP_QUALITY=78 floor 60 — each accepted upload yields roughly ≤350KB-1MB of WebP in R2.
ChatSendSerializer.image FileField optional; validate() allows image-only messages (body optional when image present, lines 71-75) — pure attachment spam needs no text.
chat_enabled gate: staff always; customers need suscription.grants_access() and not plan_suscription.is_trial — cheapest paid plan suffices.
Representative _check_quota caller (order proofs) — confirms quota accounting exists for every other client upload path; chat is the sole gap.

conditions.description: Attacker holds an authenticated platform User account (auth.User JWT) on any paid non-trial plan granting has_support_chat — the cheapest paid tier qualifies; staff bypass the gate but are trusted.
R2 (DAVENT bucket) configured via S3_API/R2_* env — the normal production path; without it objects go to MEDIA_ROOT/private (still unbounded disk growth, nginx-blocked).
purge_personal_data cron actually scheduled with some --days (default 365) — determines real retention bound; if unscheduled, attachments persist indefinitely. Unresolved deployment fact.
Sustained automated uploads; with no effective rate limit the only practical bound is request throughput and per-file ~350KB-1MB output size.

execution.attacker_perspective: A paying DAVENT customer (or anyone who buys the cheapest plan) wanting to inflate operator-owned R2 storage costs / bucket size, or to burn synchronous Pillow CPU on gunicorn workers, via the support-chat attachment path.
payloads: POST /api/chat/send/ multipart/form-data {image: <valid PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF <=4MB>} repeated in a loop — body optional, image-only messages accepted
GET /api/chat/send/ is not needed; each POST returns 201 with the serialized message
instructions: Purchase/activate any paid non-trial plan so chat_enabled(request.user) passes.
Loop POST /api/chat/send/ with a valid image file (e.g., a 4MB PNG that normalizes to ~350KB-1MB WebP at 1600px).
Observe 201 responses with no 429 — ChatSendThrottle is dead (no view.throttle_scope) and throttle_classes replaced the default user throttle.
Each iteration creates one R2 object 'chat/<thread>/<uuid>.webp' plus one ChatMessage row; repeat indefinitely — nothing decrements or caps any counter.
Confirm no quota surface exists: storage_payload/used_bytes belong to Store rows and are untouched by chat keys.
execution.observed_result: Source-derived (read-only audit): each accepted upload produces a WebP object in the DAVENT R2 bucket with no increment/decrement of any quota counter and no rate-limit check (ScopedRateThrottle.allow_request returns True because no view defines throttle_scope). ChatMessage rows and R2 objects accumulate until the annual purge_personal_data run (if scheduled).

remediation.strategy: Add a bounded budget for chat attachments: count attachment bytes in a per-user or per-plan quota (extend storage_used_bytes-style accounting or a dedicated usage table checked+consumed under lock in upload_chat_image), cap total attachments per thread/user, and shorten attachment retention. Separately fix the dead throttles: ScopedRateThrottle requires view.throttle_scope — either set throttle_scope='chat_send'/'chat' on the viewset actions or switch ChatPollThrottle/ChatSendThrottle to SimpleRateThrottle subclasses with get_cache_key keyed by user.pk (same fix pattern as feed/support). Audit NotificationPollThrottle (AdminApp/domains/notifications) for the identical bug.

likelihood.reason: Requires a paid non-trial account (real but low-cost barrier — the cheapest plan qualifies) plus scripted automation; once obtained there is NO effective rate limit at all (the 120/h throttle is dead code), so sustained abuse is trivial.

impact.reason: Operator-owned R2 storage spend and bucket growth plus synchronous Pillow CPU per request; per-file output ~350KB-1MB and input capped at 4MB/1600px. Slow-burn cost/resource issue with no cross-tenant data exposure; retention bounded to ~1 year if the purge cron runs.

confidence.reason: Missing quota fully source-verified (zero quota references in attachments.py; _STORE_KEY_RE bypass confirmed; _check_quota callers enumerated — all store-scoped). The dead-throttle discovery is deterministic from vendored DRF source plus a repo-wide grep showing zero throttle_scope definitions. Only residual uncertainty is deployment-side: whether purge_personal_data is scheduled and with what --days, and whether R2 env is configured — both noted as conditions, neither affects the missing-bound verdict.
